title: Cachekey normalization, shard affinity and staged-apply safety playbook
creator: Amelia Chen
description:
Goal: reduce per-token serving cost by increasing effective KV cache hit-rate while keeping tail latency and correctness risk bounded. This ticket delivers (1) a canonical cache-key normalization layer, (2) a shard-affinity policy to keep hot prefixes co-located, and (3) a staged-apply + circuit-breaker playbook for safe config rollout and automated rollback.

Scope: prototype and validate normalization rules (lowercasing, safe trimming, prefix canonicalization, deterministic hashing), implement per-prefix affinity hints in cache placement service, build a simulator to estimate hit-rate delta under real prefix frequency distributions, and create an operator-visible staged-apply flow (canaries, ramp, automated rollback on defined signals).

Approach: we will run offline hit-modeling using weekly prefix histograms from Console (7-day windows) and a synthetic sampler to measure how normalization and affinity affect cross-shard miss amplification. For TTL policy tuning we will generate three candidate tiers (short/medium/long) driven by per-prefix frequency percentiles and retention cost curves. A config generator will emit a candidate policy and a recommended rollout profile (canary size, ramp steps, thresholds).

Safety model and rollback: staged-apply flow enforces: initial 1% canary, 10% step ramps with 12h observation windows, automated rollback if (a) prefix-level miss-rate increases > 6% absolute for any top-100 prefix, or (b) p95 latency regression > 20ms sustained for 3 consecutive windows, or (c) error-rate increase > 0.1%. Rollback is automated via feature-flag reversal and an exponential backoff for re-attempts. All decisions are logged to the rollout audit channel and tied to the release.

Success criteria: net cache hit-rate uplift >= 3% on production workloads for target tenants, cost-per-generated-token reduction >= 4% measured over 14d post-rollout, no sustained p95 latency regressions or increased error-rate.

Trade-offs and notes: normalization can over-canonicalize (risk of conflating rare prefixes), so rule set includes a whitelist/blacklist and per-tenant opt-outs. Shard affinity reduces cross-shard misses but may increase load imbalance; autoscaler policy must accept short-term imbalance during ramp. Some tenants with strict isolation will be excluded from affinity placement.

Next steps: finish simulator runs for top-20 tenants (ETA 2025-03-07), land normalization library PR, add affinity hints proto and feature flag scaffolding, and prepare rollout dashboard tiles with per-prefix heatmaps.

2025-02-28 - Architecture sync: will implement affinity hints as a soft preference in placement service; autoscaler team (ENG-1198) to accept transient imbalance via temporary overprovisioning flag.

2025-03-03 - Drafted safety thresholds. Security asked for auditability on rollback; added audit event payloads and Confluence doc link. Planning staged canary 1% -> 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 12h windows.
